title: How Sex and Gender Differences Influence Functional Recovery in Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury: A Systematic Review.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to examine how sex differences and, when available, gender-related factors affect rehabilitation outcomes in individuals with TBI.
DESIGN: Systematic review registered in PROSPERO (ID: 1018531) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook. We included randomized controlled trials and observational and experimental studies published in the past 5 years (2020-2025) that explicitly analyzed sex- and/or gender-related differences in response to a rehabilitation intervention after TBI.
INTERVENTIONS: Various rehabilitation programs, including conventional therapy, virtual reality, and telerehabilitation.
MAIN MEASURES: Cognitive, motor, emotional, functional, and social outcomes, analyzed by biological sex and, when available, gender-related psychosocial traits.
RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria. Most findings referred to sex-based differences: female participants (sex: female) demonstrated better recovery in cognitive and social functioning, potentially linked to neuroprotective effects of estrogen and progesterone. However, they also reported higher anxiety and more persistent postconcussive symptoms. Only one study investigated gender as a social construct, suggesting that gender-related social traits, particularly those culturally associated with femininity, were associated with reduced access to rehabilitation services. A subset of studies evaluated technology-assisted interventions (e.g., virtual reality, telerehabilitation); however, sex/gender-differential effects were rarely tested, limiting firm conclusions about tailoring by sex or gender.
CONCLUSIONS: Although current evidence predominantly concerns sex-based differences, limited data also point to a potential role of gender-related social factors. Together, these findings suggest that sex and gender may significantly shape rehabilitation outcomes after TBI. Integrating sex- and gender-sensitive strategies into clinical pathways may improve equity, enhance personalization, and optimize recovery. Standardized, gender-inclusive protocols are needed to address disparities and promote fair access to neurorehabilitation.

标题：性别与性别差异如何影响创伤性脑损伤患者的功能恢复：一项系统综述
摘要：目的：本系统综述旨在探讨性别差异以及（在可用时）性别相关因素如何影响创伤性脑损伤患者的康复结局。设计：在PROSPERO注册（ID: 1018531）并遵循PRISMA指南及Cochrane手册进行的系统综述。我们纳入过去5年（2020-2025年）发表的、明确分析创伤性脑损伤后康复干预中性与/或性别相关差异的随机对照试验、观察性及实验性研究。干预措施：多种康复计划，包括常规治疗、虚拟现实及远程康复。主要测量指标：按生理性别及（在可用时）性别相关社会心理特征分析的认知、运动、情感、功能及社会结局。结果：六项研究符合纳入标准。多数发现涉及性别差异：女性参与者（生理性别为女性）在认知和社会功能方面表现出更好的恢复，这可能与雌激素和孕激素的神经保护作用有关。然而，她们也报告了更高的焦虑及更持续的脑震荡后症状。仅有一项研究将性别作为社会建构进行探讨，表明性别相关社会特质（尤其是文化上与女性气质相关的特质）与康复服务获取减少相关。部分研究评估了技术辅助干预（如虚拟现实、远程康复）的效果；然而，极少检验性别差异效应，因此难以就按性别或性别差异定制干预得出确切结论。结论：尽管当前证据主要关涉性别差异，但有限数据也指向性别相关社会因素的潜在作用。总体而言，这些发现表明性别与性别可能显著影响创伤性脑损伤后的康复结局。将性别敏感策略整合到临床路径中可能改善公平性、增强个性化并优化恢复。需要制定标准化、包容性别的方案，以解决差异并促进神经康复的公平可及性。
关键词：创伤性脑损伤；性别差异；性别因素；功能恢复；系统综述
